To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the C4/CBP ratio is a sensitive and specific predictor of complement activation and inflammatory responses in whole blood incubation with artificial surfaces.

(1) C4/C4B ratio is a sensitive and specific predictor of complement-mediated inflammatory response; (2) C4/CB ratio can predict complement-mediated inflammatory response in whole blood; (3) C4/CBP ratio correlates with downstream inflammatory response, i.e. cytokine generation; and (4) C4/C3BP ratio is a robust predictor of biocompatiblity with superior specificity and sensitiity over the current gold standards.

the C4/CBP ratio in blood incubated with a material is a robust predictor of biocompatibi- lity with superior specificity and sensi- tivity compared to the current gold standard (complement activation products).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel methods for predicting inflammatory responses to biomaterials.
the development of a new test method to predict the inflammatory response of a patient to a biomaterial.
the development of new biomaterials and the prediction of their biocompatibility.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ratio of C3 to its inhibitor C3bBbP, C4 to its inhibitory protein C4bBbP or C4BP, or C5 to its inhibitors C5bC6C7 or C5bC8, is a better predictor of biocompatible surfaces than the current gold standard, the generation of the terminal complement complex C5b-9.
the C4/CBP-ratio in plasma is a robust predictor of the biocompatibility of biomaterials.
the protein fingerprint of adsorbed proteins in plasma is a better predictor of biocompatibilty than the activation of complement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C4/CBP ratio can be used to predict the biocompatibility of biomaterials in blood.
the C4/CBP ratio is a robust, predictor for complement activation in blood and a potential biomarker for biomaterials testing.
the C4/CBP ratio is a robust and sensitive predictor of biocompability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the complement system is an important factor in determining the biocompatibility of biomaterials, and it should be considered when evaluating their biocompatibility.
complement activation products are not the best predictors of biocompatibility.
complement activation is not a reliable biomarker to evaluate the biocompatibility of a biomaterial.
